chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim [from his father] from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al-Jaroud, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever I narrate to you something, ask me about it from the Book of Allah.'
Then he said in his hadith: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden the saying of "it was said" and "he said", the spoiling of wealth, and the abundance of questioning.'
So they said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, and where is this from the Book of Allah?'
He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: There is no good in most of their secret counsels — the Verse.'
And He said: And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has Made for you a (means of) support
And He said: Do not put questions about things which if declared to you may trouble you

key_terms.الْقِيلِ وَ الْقَالِ: Idle talk or gossip (literally 'it was said and he said')

ai.seo_question: How does the Quran support the prohibition of idle talk and excessive questioning in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the Quran as the ultimate criterion for validating prophetic traditions, demonstrating that the prohibition of 'al-qil wal-qal' (idle talk and gossip), wealth wastage, and excessive questioning are deeply rooted in the Divine Text. By linking these specific behavioral guidelines to verses on secret counsels, giving wealth to the foolish, and avoiding troublesome questions, he highlights the Quran's comprehensive guidance for social and spiritual discipline. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly principle that the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings are not separate from but rather an elaboration of the Quran's explicit injunctions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, and Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever I<sup>asws</sup> narrate to you all, so ask me<sup>asws</sup> about (where it is from) the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said in a Hadeeth of his<sup>asws</sup> that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Forbidden from the ‘It was said such’, and ‘he said such’, and the spoiling of the wealth, and the abundance of questioning’.
So they said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And where is this from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’
Heasws said: ‘Allah Mighty and Majestic is Saying in Hisazwj Book [4:114] There is no good in most of their secret counsels – the Verse,
and Heazwj Said [4:5] And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has Made for you a (means of) support;
and Heazwj Said [5:101] O you who believe! Do not put questions about things which if declared to you may trouble you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz who has said the following:

“‘Isma’il, son of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had a certain amount of dinar and a man from Quraysh wanted to travel to Yemen, so ‘Isma’il asked his father, ’Father, so and so wants to go to Yemen and I have so and so amount of dinar. Do you think I should give it to him to bring for me goods from Yemen?’

Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Are you not aware that he drinks wine?’ ‘Isma’il replied, ‘Yes, this is what people say about him.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Son, do not give him your dinars.’ ‘Isma’il disobeyed his father and gave the dinars to him. He used them and did not bring anything. ‘Isma’il traveled, so also abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, for al-Hajj in that year. ‘Isma’il, when performing Tawaf would say, ‘O Lord, grant me reward and replace for me what I have lost.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, approached him and tapped him with his hand and said, ‘Hold it my son, by Allah, you have no ground for your argument before Allah and you have no right for receiving any reward or replacement for what you have lost, when you knew that he drank wine and you still trusted him.’ ‘Isma’il said, ‘O father, I did not see him drinking wine. I only heard people say so.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘My son, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says in His book, “He believes in Allah and in the believers,” [9:62] meaning he accepts (the words of) Allah (as true words) and accepts (the words of) the believers (as true words). When the believers testify before you then accept their words as true and do not trust one who drinks wine;
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says in His book, “You must not give your assets to dimwitted ones.” [4:5]

Who can be more dimwitted than one who drinks wine? The speech (advice) of one who drinks wine has no beneficial effect, his intercession is useless and he is not trusted in matters of trust. Whoever entrusts him with his assets and he destroys it, such person does not deserve any reward from Allah for his loss or replacement from Allah.’”
